_meta.description: Global bottleneck archetypes for Discovery recommend step. Prefer filling bottlenecks inside each F3iche JSON; keep this file for cross-niche archetypes or until F3iches are complete.

archetypes.notes: Critical for trading/retail SMEs expanding warehouses. Serialized items must use Stock Entry (Material Receipt) for opening balances, as standard Stock Reconciliation only updates quantity, not serial numbers.

archetypes.primary_bottleneck: Manufacturing BOM and Finished Goods Valuation Disconnect
archetypes.notes: Tally migrants frequently struggle here due to the shift to relational WIP tracking. Ensure secondary item valuation logic is strictly defined in Day-1 training to prevent stock adjustment ledger dumping.
Essential bottleneck to resolve to bridge the gap between sales demand and warehouse supply. Defer complex RFQ broadcasting and supplier scoring on Day 1 to reduce user adoption friction.

Critical data migration architectural warning: Implementation MUST use Sales Invoice with 'is_opening' flag to preserve aging histories, rather than processing a bulk Journal Entry against the customer ledger.

archetypes.primary_bottleneck: Unstructured Field Service Dispatching and SLA Failure
archetypes.notes: NEW ARCHETYPE SUGGESTED - REQUIRES ENGINEERING APPROVAL. Crucial structural mapping for facility management and field service SMEs that are completely reliant on consumer messaging apps.

archetypes.primary_bottleneck: Subcontractor Job Work Yield Leakage and Statutory Reclassifications (Section 143)
archetypes.notes: NEW ARCHETYPE SUGGESTED - REQUIRES ENGINEERING APPROVAL. Essential for OEM Tier-1 suppliers and process manufacturers. Standard Tally users only track ledger balances (e.g., job work service expenses) and completely fail to track physical raw material balances sitting at third-party job workers. This leads to massive scrap leaking and statutory compliance failure under Section 143 of the CGST Act (1-year limit for inputs, 3-year limit for capital goods, after which it is treated as a deemed supply). Implementation must seed the Subcontracting Order and Subcontracting Receipt doctypes (introduced in ERPNext v14) to bypass the classic v13 PO stock-item limitation.

archetypes.primary_bottleneck: Unstructured B2B Return Merchandise Authorization and Serialized Warranty Tracking
archetypes.notes: NEW ARCHETYPE SUGGESTED - REQUIRES ENGINEERING APPROVAL. Crucial for manufacturing and distribution SMEs handling high-value serialized equipment. Standard ERPNext requires significant customization to capture both the incoming faulty serial number and the outgoing replacement serial number on the same transaction. SMEs migrating from basic accounting systems (like Tally) struggle with reverse inventory valuation and GST compliance on free-of-cost replacement spares. Seeding 'Warranty Claim' and 'Maintenance Visit' on Day 1 is mandatory; avoid over-complicating with preventive 'Maintenance Schedule' until reactive flows are stable.

archetypes.primary_bottleneck: Multi-Tier Rule-Based Sales Commission and Accounts Payable Desynchronization
signals: partner is not created as vendor
archetypes.notes: NEW ARCHETYPE SUGGESTED - REQUIRES ENGINEERING APPROVAL. A massive systemic gap for trading and distribution SMEs. Tally does not handle automated commissions, and ERPNext does not auto-generate Accounts Payable for Sales Partners by default. Implementation must link the Sales Partner to a Supplier record to enable standard Payment Entry workflows, bypassing manual, error-prone Journal Entries. Defer advanced tiered accelerators and payroll integration on Day 1; focus on establishing the basic invoice-to-payable liability ledger.

archetypes.primary_bottleneck: E-Way Bill Transit Compliance Desynchronization and Detention Liability Risks
archetypes.notes: NEW ARCHETYPE SUGGESTED - REQUIRES ENGINEERING APPROVAL. Highly critical for Indian trading and manufacturing SMEs dispatching FTL or LTL consignments. Under Section 129 of the CGST Act, transit without valid documentation (like missing Ship-To GSTIN for Bill-To/Ship-To setups or expired validity) triggers a 200% tax penalty and physical vehicle detention. Since the June 15, 2026 mandate, the Ship-To GSTIN is strictly required and cannot be blank. Day-1 setup must map multiple customer addresses with correct GSTINs and use Delivery Note as the baseline document for Part-B validation before dispatch.
